# What is the pipe (`%>%`)?

.pull-left[
- comes from the `magrittr` package

- loaded automatically with the super package `tidyverse`

- makes code concise:
  * streamlining many operations into fewer LOC
  
  * reduces repetitive tasks
]

.pull-right[ ![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8f/Trans-Alaska_Pipeline_System_Luca_Galuzzi_2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)
]

# What is the pipe (`%>%`)?

.pull-left[
  
- makes code concise:
  * streamlining many operations into fewer LOC
  
  * reduces repetitive tasks
  
```{r}
iris <- group_by(iris,Species)

```

# What is the pipe (`%>%`)?

.pull-left[

- makes code concise:
  * streamlining many operations into fewer LOC
  
  * reduces repetitive tasks
  
```{r}
iris <- group_by(iris,Species)
summarise(iris,mean_length=mean(Sepal.Length))
```
]

.pull-right[
```{r}
iris%>%
  group_by(Species)%>%
  summarize(mean_length=mean(Sepal.Length))

```
]



---

# What is the pipe (`%>%`)?

.pull-left[

- more apparent when plotting (major piece of data science)


```{r,fig.height=3,eval=FALSE}
iris <- group_by(iris,Species)
iris_mean <- summarise(iris,mean_length=mean(Sepal.Length))

ggplot(data=iris_mean,aes(x=Species,y=mean_length))+geom_bar(stat="identity")

```
]


.pull-right[
```{r,fig.height=3}
iris%>%
  group_by(Species)%>%
  summarize(mean_length=mean(Sepal.Length))%>%
  ggplot(aes(x=Species,y=mean_length))+
  geom_bar(stat="identity")
  
```
]

# Loading data

- `readr` package has several handy functions.

- `read_csv()` most handy

```{r,fig.height=3,message=FALSE}
d <- read_csv("https://bcorgbio.github.io/class/data/coyote.csv")
head(d)
```

---

# Loading data


```{r,fig.height=3}
d%>%
  group_by(state)%>%
  dplyr::summarize(n=n())%>%
  ggplot(aes(x=state,y=n))+geom_bar(stat="identity")+coord_flip()
  
```
